title: Steelers rout Broncos two days after releasing Aaron Rodgers
excerpt: Pittsburgh thrashed Denver 27-5 on Black Friday after cutting Aaron Rodgers, who publicly attacked coach Mike McCarthy over his benching.
content_html:
The Pittsburgh Steelers beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Friday (US time), two days after releasing quarterback Aaron Rodgers following a bitter public split with head coach Mike McCarthy.

How the split unfolded

The week began with the club saying Rodgers would stay as starter despite a two-game losing streak. On Tuesday night the Steelers announced instead that he was benched for the Denver game and would be inactive, with Mason Rudolph to start.

Rodgers appeared on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and said he would not return to the team. "That ship has sailed," he said.

He said McCarthy never told him about the benching and that he heard about it from teammate Pat Freiermuth. Rodgers also alleged that McCarthy had fallen asleep in meetings, missed walk-throughs and declined to watch game film. He described the coach as unwell.

The Steelers announced that afternoon that Rodgers had been released.

McCarthy, who coached Rodgers in Green Bay from 2006 to 2018, denied holding a grudge from their time together. He defended both the benching and his own fitness for the job.

The game

On the field, Pittsburgh dominated. Linebacker T.J. Watt recovered a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone for a touchdown, and cornerback Jalen Ramsey returned an interception for another. Rudolph completed nine of 15 passes for 142 yards and threw a touchdown to DK Metcalf.

The win lifted Pittsburgh to 7-4 and kept them unbeaten at home this season. It also ended Denver's six-game winning streak and left the Broncos at 8-3. According to CBS Sports, it was the first 27-5 result in NFL history.

Rodgers was not finished with the story. During the Amazon Prime Video broadcast, he texted play-by-play commentator Al Michaels and claimed the team had barred him from its training facility after the benching.

A record career

Rodgers went into this season as the NFL's all-time leader in touchdown-to-interception ratio and career passer rating, and fourth on the all-time list for passing touchdowns with 527. He rejoined Pittsburgh in May, reuniting with McCarthy, who became the Steelers' coach in January after Mike Tomlin stepped down.

What's next

Rodgers, 42, had already said in May that 2026 would be his 22nd and final NFL season. The four-time league MVP is now a free agent. Whether he plays again this season is unclear.
